obtained.how: Internet Archive, public download without login: the whole October 1977 issue (vol. 34 no. 10, the PERCIS symposium issue) from its Serials in Microfilm collection; the article is PDF pp. 480–493. Table 1's values are missing from the scan's OCR layer, so they were read from the page image (rendered locally)

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the title page ("J. Fish. Res. Board Can. 34: 1922-1935")
bibliography.note: issue 10 per the Internet Archive item and Crossref; part of the Proceedings of the Percid International Symposium (PERCIS)

claims.claim: adult and juvenile sets (Kitchell et al. 1977; CTO 23 and 29 °C)
claims.source_value: 23 °C is the optimum for "juveniles and adults"; 29 °C is for "young-of-year" only (used for first-year growth)
claims.quote: Optimum temperature for consumption young-of-year 29°C juveniles and adults 23°C
claims.conditions: parameters estimated from the literature, mostly Perca fluviatilis laboratory data (Solomon & Brafield 1972) assumed to apply to P. flavescens
claims.note: label the 29 °C set young-of-year, not juvenile (FB4 calls it "juvenile"). The code applies it to fish under a year old (world.js:49), which matches the source

claims.claim: FB4 yellow perch adult set: CA 0.25, CB −0.27, CQ 2.3, CTO 23, CTM 28; RB −0.2, RQ 2.1, RTO 28, RTM 33; SDA 0.15; ACT 1; FA 0.158, FB −0.222, FG 0.631; UA 0.0292, UB 0.58, UG −0.299
claims.quote: Intercept for maximum consumption 0.25 Slope for maximum consumption −0.27
claims.conditions: per-day rates in biomass equivalents; Winberg I activity ("all simulations presented herein assume a Winberg I model (A = 1.0)"); egestion/excretion from Elliott's brown trout equations fitted to P. fluviatilis eating Gammarus at 14 °C; the 28 °C consumption maximum and respiration optimum were "arbitrarily chosen" as the midpoint of 23 and 33 °C

claims.source_value: a2 = 0.035, the maximum standard respiration of a 1-g fish as a proportion of body weight per day (biomass equivalents)
claims.conditions: respiration at the optimum temperature for respiration, standard (Winberg I) level
claims.note: 0.0108 is not printed here: it equals 0.035 × 4,186 J/g ÷ 13,560 J/g O₂ (project arithmetic), i.e. FB4's conversion to g O₂ g⁻¹ d⁻¹. The model value is consistent; only the attribution should say "as converted in FB4"

claims.paper: src/species.js:290 (ED 4186 in the set labelled Kitchell et al. 1977)
claims.note: the model is written in biomass equivalents and gives no energy density; 4,186 J/g (1 kcal/g) must come from FB4 or elsewhere

claims.claim: juvenile set CTO 29, CTM 32, RTO 32, RTM 35
claims.quote: Maximum temperature for standard respiration young-of-year 35°C juveniles and adults 33°C
claims.conditions: young-of-year values; "young-of-the-year fish were used for first-year growth", all older fish physiologically adult (p. 1931)

claims.claim: Kitchell consumption-temperature curve: warm-water, peaks at CTO, 0 at/above CTM
claims.quote: declines rapidly to zero at the maximum temperature
claims.conditions: r_c = V^X·e^(X(1−V)), V = (Tm − T)/(Tm − To), with W and Y from ln Q, (Tm − To); maximum 1.0 at To

claims.claim: Kitchell respiration: the same curve peaking at RTO and falling to ~0 at RTM, times a constant activity multiplier ACT
claims.quote: adjustment of respiration similar to r of equation 2 but with different parameter values
claims.conditions: R = Rmax·A·r_r + S·C; A = activity multiple of standard respiration (A = 2.0 is Winberg II)

claims.claim: the yellow perch set (23 °C optimum, 28 °C cutoff) stands in for white sucker and white perch
claims.quote: Maximum temperature for consumption young-of-year juveniles and adults 32°C 28°C
claims.conditions: values for yellow perch; the stand-in use is the project's
claims.note: the source says nothing about suckers or white perch; the match to their thermal ranges is the project's argument

tried.note: OpenAlex: closed, no repository copy (publisher page for a library login)

notes: Kitchell et al. varied the egestion intercept with diet: 0.158 for invertebrate prey but 0.10 to 0.05 for fish prey in their Lake Erie runs (Table 3, p. 1931, from Kelso 1972); FB4's single FA 0.158 overstates egestion for piscivorous perch if the model uses it for all diets. Cmax was not measured for perch or walleye: a1 = 0.25 was extrapolated (Brett's method). The 23 °C optimum is from Schneider (1973) and equals the final preferendum (Neill & Magnuson 1974). The fetch came from the Internet Archive's Serials in Microfilm collection, an in-copyright journal it serves openly: the human may want to confirm that source is acceptable.
